beats.speaker: Host
beats.text: The dropped word that changes the meaning most is the absence of "withdrawn" or any synonym for it in a week where war-related topics were steady at around 10% of total stories. </think> There seems to be a notable gap in the coverage of war-related topics in terms of void words. Given that those types of events might usually draw attention, the absence of descriptive terms can be viewed as a form of narrative framing; either these wars are perceived to have "retreated" from public consciousness or they're being framed in a more passive or unnoteworthy way. Another possibility is that coverage of war topics has shifted into meta narratives, where conflict is discussed through the lens of internal processes and governance rather than through descriptive void words.
